1.pericope_label: Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff
debates: Whether the verb means to gather, to sift, to bend, or to search
Whether the nation is undesiring, undesirable, or unashamed
What the decree is that is about to be delivered
outliers: Ellicott says the familiar rendering has little to recommend it and prefers bend yourselves
Calvin rejects the reading that turns the call into ridicule of the people
Henry contrasts this summons with the later counsel to flee to the mountains
themes: A people told to gather rather than scatter
Chaff waiting for the first breath of wind
Consciences searched for the provoking sin
A decree carried to full term

3.pericope_label: Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD’S anger
debates: Whether the meek are the godly remnant or simply the afflicted
Why a people already doing his judgment are told to seek him
What it means to have wrought his judgment
outliers: Calvin says the faithful are tamed by chastisement while the wicked keep a brazen front
Gill makes the whole call to repentance issued for the sake of a remnant
Ellicott renders the clause as executed his sentence rather than did what was right
themes: A heifer that had to be broken to the yoke
Preaching that goes on though it sings to the deaf
Good and wicked struck alike in the first confusion
Ceremonies heaped up in place of a life

4.pericope_label: For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up
debates: Why the doom of the neighbours follows the call to repentance
Whether the Cherethites are Cretans, or Crete a Philistine colony
Why only four of the five cities are named
outliers: Henry says the wrongful holding of land granted to Israel is now remembered against them
Gill reverses the usual descent and makes Crete the colony rather than the parent
Calvin reads the whole oracle as consolation addressed to the remnant
themes: A city taken at noon because it is not worth surprising by night
Names that turn into their own sentence
A royal bodyguard drawn from a doomed people
Comfort found in having companions in woe

6.pericope_label: And the sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks. And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah
debates: Whether the disputed word means cisterns, dug caves, pastures, or a place-name
When the coast came into the hands of the remnant
Whether the visiting is for relief or for punishment
outliers: Clarke reports a proposal to read the word as the name of a country rather than a shelter
Ellicott finds the same term meaning both sea coast and apportioned inheritance
Calvin uses the remnant to keep a small congregation from despising itself
themes: Warehouses replaced by a few huts
Shepherds sleeping in caves cut into the hills
Grass growing where no one sows
A ruined coast handed over as an inheritance

8.pericope_label: I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border
debates: Whether the opening words are spoken by God or by the faithful
How far the likeness to Sodom is meant to extend
Which devastation of Moab the threat points to
outliers: Calvin says one reproach carries more bitterness than a hundred deaths
Henry turns the hearing of God into a reason for the injured to stay silent
Ellicott dates the ruin later than the devastation the histories record
themes: Kinsmen who turned out the cruellest neighbours
Insults kept in a book of remembrance
An oath sworn by the life of the one swearing
Brambles and salt-pits where towns had stood

10.pericope_label: This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD of hosts. Ye Ethiopians also, ye shall be slain by my sword
debates: Whether the Lord is terrible to Moab or to be feared by his own people
Whether the nations worship at Jerusalem or each in his own place
Which Ethiopians are meant, and by whose sword
outliers: Ellicott finds here one of the very few promises of worship offered outside the Holy Land
Clarke explains the famishing of the gods from the belief that they fed on the smoke of sacrifice
Calvin argues from the punishment of the remote nation to the certainty of the near one
themes: Pride named as the first sin of all
Idols starved of the smoke they lived on
Distance no hindrance to a name being celebrated
A conqueror serving as a sword he does not own

13.pericope_label: And he will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness
debates: Whose hand is stretched out against the north
Whether Nineveh fell at a stroke or decayed by degrees
Which birds and beasts the two Hebrew words name
outliers: Calvin makes Moab and Ammon mere fans who stirred up stronger nations
Ellicott quotes a song bird singing in the windows of a city whose name once made the world pale
Clarke sets a Persian couplet on ruined palaces beside the prophecy
themes: A city whose very site is now unknown
Cedar ceilings left open to the rain
Wild beasts arriving from remote places
Sheep lying down where crowds once walked

15.pericope_label: This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in!
debates: Whether the closing words are the prophet’s or those of passers-by
What made the city secure enough to speak so
Whether the language is borrowed from an earlier prophecy
outliers: Calvin says the greatness the city boasted of was itself the cause of its fall
Ellicott derives the boast from words spoken earlier against another city
Calvin has the swollen wall fall without anyone pushing it
themes: A city that thought itself built in the clouds
Mirth that went on without interruption
A passer-by waving a hand at a ruin
A condition assumed to be permanent
